correctness.rationale: The published geometric-semilattice wedge theorem applies to every k. A direct disjoint counting of chains by span and ordered increments gives the exact face polynomial; the Stirling/falling-factorial identity proves Euler and thus b_{n,k}. Consecutive levels have reduced integral homology supported in distinct degrees, so all nonterminal persistence maps vanish; terminal sphere is S^{n-2}. The supplied standard-Python checker confirms all n<=6 boundaries and counts through n<=40, not used as proof.

value.rationale: The natural open numerical problem following Kitajima’s wedge-existence theorem is to determine all sphere multiplicities and their persistence lifetimes for the fundamental Boolean test family. This claim calculates the whole integer barcode for unbounded n and all k by a uniform recurrence, not just a known k=2 slice or an arbitrary finite sample; it also distinguishes homotopy support known from exact ranks and lifespan newly counted.
